title: Asset-Referenced and E-Money Tokens
summary: How ARTs and EMTs are structured and regulated under MiCA, the reserve and redemption mechanics that determine stability, and the supervisory arrangements for significant tokens.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How ARTs and EMTs are structured and regulated under MiCA, the reserve and redemption mechanics that determine stability, and the supervisory arrangements for significant tokens.
Learning Objectives: Distinguish ART and EMT designs and their risk profiles
Evaluate reserve quality, custody and redemption resilience under stress
Explain significance classification and the EBA's supervisory role
Syllabus: Issuer authorisation, white papers and lessons from stablecoin failures
Reserve composition, custody, audit and redemption at par
EMTs, electronic money and the interplay with PSD2
Significant tokens: EBA supervision, colleges and recovery and redemption plans
Intended Audience: Authorisation, supervision and inspection staff new to crypto-asset service providers and token issuers
AML/CFT, market integrity, payments and enforcement specialists who need a working grasp of MiCA
Managers and policy staff who need an overview before committing teams to deeper training
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of authorising or supervising financial firms is helpful. No technical background in blockchain is required.
Core Reading: Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 on information accompanying transfers of funds and certain crypto-assets (Transfer of Funds Regulation)
FSB, High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Crypto-Asset Activities and Markets (2023)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
